SMTO-TSK-0055 — The Agent gave two planned steps the same name

GUID: 42715810-4222-433f-accd-73495c4df3df
Slug: dependency-identity-conflict
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The Agent planned several steps but labelled two of them the same way, or reused a label from earlier work in this task. SMTO rejected the new plan, so none of its new steps ran. Earlier steps are unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait to see whether the Agent tries again; it is told about this problem automatically. The Agent usually fixes duplicate labels on its next attempt.
  2. If the task ends with this error, read the results already shown in the conversation to see which steps finished. Earlier steps in this task still happened; only the new plan was rejected.
  3. Send a message asking the Agent to continue with only the steps that haven't been done yet. This avoids repeating work that already finished.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's remaining steps start and show results in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask the Agent to redo steps that already finished without checking their results first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Activity IDs, dependency node aliases or child call IDs in the proposed batch duplicate each other or collide with work already accepted in this run, so the whole batch was rejected.

What this means

  • Activity IDs, node aliases or child call identities duplicate each other or collide with existing claimed work. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Activity IDs, node aliases or child call identities duplicate each other or collide with existing claimed work.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare new IDs with accepted graph nodes and durable claims; existing work must retain its original identity.

How to fix it

  • Use unique ids for every item in a parallel or schedule_activities batch and do not reuse node ids already accepted in the run. Accepted nodes are immutable: inspect their receipts to decide what remains, then submit only the remaining work with new ids.
  • Use unique IDs for new operations. Keep previously accepted nodes immutable and inspect their receipts before deciding what remains.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Distinct new operations have unique IDs while accepted nodes and receipts remain unchanged.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
